title: Record plan group sizes and unplanned items in the drain report
summary: Add per-plan-group item counts and a separate unplanned count to the drain run's Report, filled for both the one-at-a-time and the parallel path, and print a group-sizes line in athena drain's summary. Goal: later runs (the maintainer) can see how much parallel work was available; this is the measurement half of build step 6.

defaults_applied.how: Tests added; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Criteria run the drain with real plans of sizes 3,1,2 and read the recorded sizes.
Doc comments and CHANGELOG written for outside readers.
One focused change to Report, the loop, display, tests, CHANGELOG.
The criterion is that later runs can read group sizes from the report and summary.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs (Report at ~1101 already holds plan_groups: Vec<Vec<String>>; the shared loop at ~2940-3070 builds the plan, takes first_plan, runs batches_for(...) groups, with one_at_a_time splitting a group to one item; drain_concurrent at ~2803 passes max_concurrency) and crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs (~701 prints 'plan        group N: ...' lines). The group sizes are measured directly from the first plan's groups (plan.groups lengths), not from how many ran at once, so they are identical for max_concurrency 1 and 2. Report is an in-memory struct with Serialize; I found no AnyRecord/check_record_file type for it under crates/athena-data, so no new record file is expected; if the producer adds a persisted record it must be covered by check_record_file/AnyRecord and the round-trip test.

Existing code: extends Report and the plan-group printing in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs and crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs, and reads Plan.groups from crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs; tests go in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs with helpers in crates/athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs.
'Drain run record' is read as the drain Report. Unplanned means a queued item that has no entry in the plan view (view.plan), counted as its own number, never as a group of 1.
Group sizes are taken from the plan the run started with (first_plan), as plan_groups already is. Items that are refused or cyclic are not counted as unplanned unless they lack a plan entry.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`: a new test drains a plan of three groups sized 3, 1 and 2 with max_concurrency 1 and asserts the report's group sizes are exactly [3, 1, 2].
A new test drains the same plan with max_concurrency 2 (drain_concurrent) and asserts the same sizes [3, 1, 2]; run with `cargo test -p athena-cli`.
A new test has a queued item with no plan entry and asserts the report counts it in a separate unplanned field (1) and that no group of size 1 is added for it.
A new test renders the drain summary (display.rs) and asserts it contains a group-sizes line such as 'group sizes 3, 1, 2' plus the unplanned count; run with `cargo test -p athena-cli`.
`cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` pass, including the existing record validation tests, so records still validate.
CHANGELOG.md gains an entry that states only what the diff does (group sizes and unplanned count in the drain report and summary), with no claim about raising max_concurrency or editing athena.toml.
The group sizes are computed in the drain loop from the plan's groups (crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs) and the field has a doc comment explaining unplanned vs group of 1.

out_of_scope: Raising max_concurrency or editing athena.toml / [drain.pipeline] (the config half of step 6)
Peak in-flight job counts and mean group size computed from many runs
Changing how the plan forms groups or how the loop dispatches them
departures: Slightly higher cost: drain.rs is very large and the tests need a two-path fixture.
